occupations.definition: Aircraft loader loads and unloads aircraft cargo. He/she stows cargo according to size, weight, type and destination of goods, following general loading instructions and unloads cargo from aircraft onto tractors. He/she lifts, transfers, arranges and secures baggage and cargo onto aircraft according to loading plans. He/she may weigh cargo before loading and keep records of loaded and unloaded items, secure cargo with tie-ropes or other fastenings and pad articles to prevent breakage.

occupations.title: Warehouse worker
occupations.definition: Warehouse worker carries and stacks goods in a warehouse, market or similar establishment. He/she loads, unloads and propels hand trucks, and stores articles in bins and on shelves according to instructions. He/she may load or unload road trucks or wagons, operate a conveyor, elevator or stacking machine, pack and weigh materials and mark information on them for identification.

occupations.title: Vehicle attendant
occupations.definition: Vehicle attendant travels with and assists vehicle drivers during the transportation of goods from one place to another. He/she loads and unloads goods onto and from the vehicle, travels in vehicles guarding goods in transit, signals traffic following the vehicle to overtake when road is clear, and washes and cleans the vehicle. He/she may assist vehicle drivers in doing minor repairs.

occupations.title: Mover
occupations.definition: Mover physically hands goods and belongings to be relocated or transported from one place to the other. He/she disassembles goods, machinery or belongings for transportation and assembles or installs them in the new location. He/she also ensures that objects are well protected and packed, secured and placed correctly in transport.

occupations.title: Lashing worker
occupations.definition: Lashing worker performs lashing and unlashing operations on board vessels. He/she also performs vessel berthing and unberthing, and container reefer plugging and unplugging operations.

occupations.title: Material/Freight handling worker n.e.c.
occupations.definition: This group covers material/freight handling worker not elsewhere classified.

occupations.title: Kitchen assistant
occupations.definition: Kitchen assistant assists in simple food preparation tasks and performs general cleaning duties in kitchen. He/she may also assist in stocktaking and storage of ingredients and beverages.
exclusions: Food and beverage (F&B) establishment general cleaner, see 91151

occupations.title: Food/Drink stall assistant
occupations.definition: Food/Drink stall assistant prepares simple food/drink items from food/drink counters or steam tables in food stalls. He/she may also assist in serving customers and in general duties including collecting payment and/or cleaning in the establishment.

occupations.title: Fast food preparer
occupations.definition: Fast food preparer prepares and cooks food in a fast food restaurant usually with a limited menu. He/she prepares and cooks basic food items using various large-volume and single-purpose cooking equipment.

occupations.title: Tea server/steward (excluding bartender, barista and food/drink stall assistant)
occupations.definition: Tea server/steward (excluding bartender, barista and food/drink stall assistant) serves tea and coffee.

sub_major_groups.title: WASTE COLLECTION, RECYCLING AND MATERIAL RECOVERY WORKERS AND OTHER ELEMENTARY WORKERS

unit_groups.title: Waste Collection, Recycling and Material Recovery Supervisors

occupations.title: Waste collection/recycling/material recovery supervisor
occupations.definition: Waste collection/recycling/material recovery supervisor supervise the activities of a unit performing various general waste and recyclables collection tasks. He/she may also undertake similar tasks as those performed by the waste and recyclables collection workers.

minor_groups.title: WASTE COLLECTION, RECYCLING AND MATERIAL RECOVERY WORKERS

unit_groups.title: Waste Collection, Recycling and Material Recovery Workers

occupations.title: General waste collection/recycling/material recovery worker
occupations.definition: General waste collection/recycling/material recovery worker collects general waste and recyclables from bins and loads them onto collection vehicles.

occupations.title: Waste recycling sorter
occupations.definition: Waste recycling sorter sorts recyclable materials and waste from a recycling stream, ensures no unsuitable materials wind up among the recyclable materials and processes recyclables in a material recovery process chain. He/she inspects the materials and performs cleaning duties, and works in compliance with waste regulations. He/she also Identifies and sets aside items of furniture, equipment, machinery, or components that are suitable for repair, reuse or recycling.

occupations.title: Waste collection/recycling/material recovery worker n.e.c.
occupations.definition: This group covers waste collection/recycling/material recovery worker not elsewhere classified.

occupations.title: Bell captain
occupations.definition: Bell captain coordinates all bell services such as luggage service and storage, message service and assigning work duties and schedules of bell staff. He/she communicates and interacts with guests, and attends to their enquiries and complaints effectively. He/she also oversees the grooming of bell staff and coaches them on their performance and all aspects of bell service.

occupations.title: Bellboy/Hotel porter
occupations.definition: Bellboy/Hotel porter greets guests, directs them to the check-in desk, escorts them and carries their luggage to their designated rooms. He/she ensures the safety and security of all guests’ belongings and manages mails, faxes and couriered items. He/she also explains the amenities and facilities of the property’s room to guests. He/she may be required to run errands or perform supporting duties for other departments.

occupations.title: Porter (excluding hotel)
occupations.definition: Porter (excluding hotel) handles baggage for travellers at transportation terminals.

occupations.title: Office/Library attendant
occupations.definition: Office/Library attendant collects and distributes files and runs errands within office. He/she maintains the cleanliness of office, collects mail from post office, addresses and seals envelopes prior to posting them.

occupations.title: Laboratory attendant
occupations.definition: Laboratory attendant cleans laboratory equipment, such as glassware, metal instruments, sinks, tables, and test panels, using solvents, brushes and rags. He/she may sterilise glassware and instruments, label tubes and bottles and fill them with specified solutions and deliver supplies and laboratory specimens to designated work areas.

occupations.title: Hospital/Clinic attendant
occupations.definition: Hospital/Clinic attendant assists in care of hospital patients under the direction of nursing and medical staff. He/she bathes, dresses patients, serves and collects food trays, feeds patients requiring help and transports patients to treatment units using wheel-chair or wheeled carriage or assists them to walk. He/she also dusts and cleans patients’ room, cleans, sterilises, stores, prepares and issues dressing packs, treatment trays and other supplies.

occupations.title: Car park attendant
occupations.definition: Car park attendant supervises the parking of vehicles in private and public car-parks. He/she records the time of entry and exit, calculates and collects parking fee, issues receipts and records particulars of vehicles and reports non-payment of fees.

occupations.title: Sports/Recreational attendant
occupations.definition: Sports/Recreational attendant performs a variety of duties at amusement or recreation facility. He/she schedules the use of recreation facilities, maintains and provides equipment to participants of sporting events or recreational pursuits, or operates amusement concessions and rides.

occupations.title: Bus attendant
occupations.definition: Bus attendant monitors the activities on buses to ensure and supervise the students’ safety and good behaviour. He/she assists students in boarding/alighting at various stops and supports the driver and provides assistance in case of emergency.

occupations.title: Restroom attendant
occupations.definition: Restroom attendant cleans and maintains toilet facilities before, during and after operational service hours, in accordance with company standards and policies. He/she uses cleaning equipment to clean mirrors, floors, toilets and sinks, refills the facility with supplies as needed and maintains records of daily operations.

occupations.title: Attendant n.e.c.
occupations.definition: This group covers attendant not elsewhere classified.

occupations.title: Building caretaker
occupations.definition: Building caretaker takes care of building. He/she guards against any theft or illegal entry. He/she may keep surroundings clean and tidy and sweep interior and exterior of building.

occupations.title: Doorman
occupations.definition: Doorman provides personal service for patrons or guests of a hotel or similar establishment by opening doors, hailing taxi-cabs, and assisting persons into and out of motor vehicles. He/she may help guests with luggage or provide other personal services.

occupations.title: Building caretaker and related worker n.e.c.
occupations.definition: This group covers building caretaker and related worker not elsewhere classified.

occupations.title: Chief concierge (hotel)
occupations.definition: Chief concierge (hotel) manages all aspects of the concierge operations to ensure that the team is functioning in accordance with the hotel’s policies and standards. He/she serves the needs of guests, runs errands, handles luggage, coordinates guest requests with designated vendors and carries out special requests such as wedding proposals or anniversaries when required. He/she also sets departmental goals, manages the inventories, daily roster, training, discipline and performance of concierge team members. He/she informs and updates other departments of concierge services and ensures that departments are aware of guests’ needs.

occupations.title: Concierge (hotel)
occupations.definition: Concierge (hotel) serves as the point of contact for property guests by providing guidance and assistance during their stay. He/she anticipates and meets the needs of guests, makes reservations, plans special events, parties and meetings, delivers luggage and mail and provides information about local shopping, dining, nightlife and recreational activities. He/she also performs secretarial and office duties, lobby maintenance, and supports other departments as required.

occupations.title: Leaflet/Newspaper distributor/deliverer
occupations.definition: Leaflet/Newspaper distributor/deliverer hands out newspapers or flyers, leaflets and advertisements either directly to the people on the streets or via mailboxes.

occupations.title: Meter reader/Vending-machine collector
occupations.definition: Meter reader/Vending-machine collector reads electric or water consumption meters and records volume used by residential and commercial consumers, and removes cash and conducts visual inspections of vending-machines. He/she takes reading of meter dials, checks readings to locate abnormal consumption and records reasons for fluctuations. He/she also inspects meters and connections for defects, damage and unauthorised connections and indicates irregularities on forms for necessary action. He/she refills goods sold for vending and other coin-operated machines and may carry out basic maintenance.

occupations.title: Odd job person
occupations.definition: Odd job person performs tasks of a simple and routine nature that usually require physical effort. He/she lifts, carries, moves and stacks heavy materials, digs holes or trenches using pick or shovel, removes waste material from working areas, sweeps roads and collects garbage.

occupations.title: Other elementary worker n.e.c.
occupations.definition: This group covers other elementary worker not elsewhere classified.

occupations.title: Worker reporting unidentifiable or inadequately described occupation
occupations.definition: This group covers persons reporting occupations which cannot be identified, occupations not sufficiently well described to permit classification in one of the preceding major groups and occupations not classifiable elsewhere because of erroneous reporting or for other reasons.

occupations.title: Worker not reporting any occupation
occupations.definition: This group covers those not reporting any information as to their occupation.

occupations.title: Singapore armed forces personnel
occupations.definition: This group covers personnel who are serving in the armed forces, including auxiliary services, whether on a voluntary or involuntary basis. Included are regular members of the army, navy, air force and other military services, as well as temporary members enrolled for full-time training or other services.

occupations.title: Foreign armed forces personnel
occupations.definition: This group covers members of foreign armed forces based in Singapore.

occupations.title: Foreign diplomatic personnel
occupations.definition: This group covers foreign diplomats and consular representatives such as ambassadors, high commissioners, attachés, etc.
